_README: Every number here is an ASSUMPTION, not measured from the NMIS file. Death rates are now ROUGHLY anchored to published Borana drought herd losses (about 30-60% of cattle lost over a severe drought episode of ~12 months, i.e. ~3-6% per month on average across the herd; thin animals die first). Weight/condition -> price effect comes from the NMIS thin/medium/fat price gap. Replace with local figures when you have them.
_threshold_meaning: Read as 'expected loss from waiting': under 1% = effectively no reason to sell (monthly price noise in the data is ~13%, so smaller differences mean nothing); 1-6% -> sell 25%; 6-15% -> sell 50%; more than 15% -> sell 75%. These are policy choices to agree with herders and experts, not measured values.
_drift_note: A rolling backtest showed the estimated monthly price drift did NOT beat a simple 'no change' forecast, so drift is set to 0 by default. See reports/PRICE_BACKTEST.md.
_crash_note: The market-crash strength (price_drop_per_full_unit_of_extra_pressure) has no local evidence. It is OFF in the headline advice; the API shows what the advice would be if it were real. Set to true only after calibrating it.
